correctness.rationale: For an ideal with vertex set S and edges T, the new edges are exactly E(S) minus T, and the new vertices are V minus S and those edges' endpoints. In a two-cycle the two vertex sets cover V and induce identical edge sets. If their intersection were proper and nonempty, a crossing edge (by connectivity) would lie in exactly one induced edge set. Empty intersection forces the bipartition, with no chosen edges; full intersection requires both complementary edge sets to span as edge covers. Both converses follow from the update and the two configurations in each pair are distinct (nonempty graph and at least one edge); labeled phases must be divided out exactly once. For a wheel the two consecutive rim colors allow one or two spokes according as they agree or differ; tracing the cyclic matrix with entries 1 and 2 yields 3^r+(-1)^r. For either fixed hub color violation, its same-color rim edges form a cycle independent set, counted by L_r, including r=3. Triangles exclude the bipartition term. Independently used top-to-bottom toggles, verified by direct enumeration for all 771 connected labeled graphs on 2–5 vertices and every ideal of six wheels r=3–8; reproduced orbit counts 9,34,110,347,1064,3234. Replay: python3 -B /workspace/branches/frozen_review_replay.py 1. The finite replay supplements, not replaces, the all-size proof. Frozen scripts were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The structural classification replaces an order-ideal search by two natural graph constraints, identifying when the two dynamical mechanisms occur. Wheels systematically separate them and provide a closed all-size census and exponential scale, useful for comparing period-two behavior beyond previously tabulated stars and bipartite families. The reduction, not the Lucas identity by itself, is the payoff.
